title: Structured Output Edgecraft: Prompt Set and Regression Template
content:
Purpose:
This document is a focused prompt set and regression reporting template designed for onboarding new model variants into Redwood's serving runtime. The goal is to stress formatting behavior and JSON schema adherence in realistic-but-adversarial ways so we can detect subtle regressions in structured-output handling (escaping, ordering, optional/extra fields, numeric edge cases, and mixed-type resolution).

Scope and Intended Usage:
- Intended for use as part of model evaluation pipelines when a new model or quantization profile is added to the catalog.
- Designed to surface failures that are likely to impact downstream parsing, tooling, and product integrations (console, dedicated, and private deployments).
- Not a comprehensive semantics test: focus is on structural correctness and deterministic patterns relevant to JSON schema consumers.

How the prompt set is organized:
The prompt set is divided into categories. For each prompt we provide: a short description, the raw prompt text (what will be sent to the model), the target JSON schema snippet name, and an example canonical output for a correct response. When running, capture the raw model string, parser errors, and a normalized JSON object if the response can be parsed.

Categories (high level):
1) Whitespace and Delimiter Noise
2) Escaping and Control Characters
3) Type Ambiguity and Coercion
4) Missing / Extra Keys and Field Order Variance
5) Arrays, Nested Records and Sparsity
6) Numeric Borders (floats, large ints, exponent notation)
7) Schema Relaxation Tests (lenient vs strict)
8) Fallback and Partial Output Cases

Representative prompts (short form):
- WHITESPACE_NOISE_01: "Return a JSON object that matches this schema: { \"id\": string, \"status\": \"ok\", \"items\": [ {\"name\": string, \"qty\": integer } ] }. Intentionally include extra spaces, newlines, and tabs between tokens."
  - Expected issues: tokenization-induced stray commas, trailing commas, or unquoted keys.
  - Canonical: {\n    \"id\": \"txn_123\",\n    \"status\": \"ok\",\n    \"items\": [{\"name\": \"widget\", \"qty\": 3}]\n  }

- ESCAPE_CTRL_02: "Produce JSON for schema: {\"message\": string, \"meta\": {\"note\": string}}. Include embedded newlines, tabs, and a raw backslash sequence in the message text."
  - Target: ensure correct escaping of \n, \t and \\ so a strict JSON parser succeeds.

- TYPE_AMBIG_03: "The schema requires \"count\": integer and \"score\": number. Provide values as decimal-like strings and as words (\"5\", \"five\"). Indicate whether you are outputting numbers or strings by type."
  - Check coercion behavior: many models output numeric-looking tokens but as quoted strings. Upstream parsers may accept coercion; strict JSON schema validators will not.

- MISSING_EXTRA_04: "Return object with fields (id, user, flags). Occasionally omit 'flags' or add 'metadata' with arbitrary contents. Show both a complete object and an intentionally truncated variant."
  - Purpose: measure policy for graceful degradation and difference between strict failure vs partial acceptance.

- ARRAY_NEST_05: "Schema: items: array of arrays of records. Create cases with empty inner arrays, inconsistent record shapes, and nulls inside arrays."
  - Examine parser acceptance and whether nulls break downstream logic.

- NUMERIC_EDGE_06: "Provide very large integers (e.g. 2**60), negative exponents, and floats with many decimals. Schema expects number but some languages/systems lose precision."

- RELAX_LENIENT_07: "Run in lenient mode: allow trailing commas and unquoted keys; then run in strict mode: reject anything not valid JSON. Compare outputs."

Execution guidance for the eval harness:
- Run each prompt at 3 temperature settings: 0.0, 0.2, 0.7. Lower temps check deterministic structure; higher temps check variability under generation noise.
- Repeat each prompt 10x for statistical coverage. Record frequency of parseable JSON and frequency of schema-valid JSON.
- Capture: request_id, model, model_config (quantization, seq length cap), raw_response, parse_error (if any), parsed_json (when parseable), schema_validation_result (pass/fail with validator message).

Pass/fail criteria (suggested):
- Critical failure if parseable JSON < 95% at temp 0.0 for well-formed prompts (WHITESPACE_NOISE_01, ESCAPE_CTRL_02).
- Regression threshold: any drop >5 percentage points in schema-valid rate vs baseline for the same model version.
- Tolerated variability: for fuzzier prompts (TYPE_AMBIG_03 or RELAX_LENIENT_07), allow higher variance but flag when strict mode fails >10% at temp 0.0.

Metrics to capture in the regression report:
- parseable_rate_by_prompt: percent of runs where a strict JSON parser could parse the text.
- schema_valid_rate_by_prompt: percent passing the JSON schema validator.
- common_parse_errors: top K parse error messages (trailing comma, unescaped control, unquoted key, single-quotes, etc.).
- token_length_distribution: median and 95th percentile.
- examples_of_partial_objects: up to 5 unique partial outputs for triage.

Regression report template (text to paste into PR):
- Model: <model-name>@<revision>
- Baseline model: <baseline-model>@<revision>
- Run date: <yyyy-mm-dd>
- Harness config: temps, repeats, seq cap, quantization
- Summary: parse_rate change: <x% -> y%>, schema_valid change: <x% -> y%>
- Top 3 failure modes and representative excerpts (sanitized)
- Suggested mitigations: prompt-stabilizers, temperature policy, model revert, kernel selection change, or pre/post-parse repair.

Prompt canonization and pre/post-processing rules (recommended):
- Always wrap output request with an explicit instruction block: e.g., "Output ONLY valid JSON matching this schema; do not add commentary."
- Use a deterministic system message for chat-based models to lock behavior.
- Optionally apply a lightweight post-processor that: removes non-JSON prefix/suffix, attempts common repairs (strip trailing commas, convert single-quotes to double), and re-validate. Record repairs applied. Repairs count as degraded results for regression scoring.

Notes on model-specific quirks discovered historically:
- Some quantized variants introduce stray line-breaks inside strings for long sequences — increase seq cap and add explicit "no line breaks in strings" directive.
- Multilingual models sometimes substitute Unicode lookalikes for quotes — add a normalization step to replace common quirks.

Checklist before adding a model to catalog (onboarding gate):
- run full prompt set at temp 0.0 and 0.2, 10 repeats each
- parseable_rate >= 95% for core formatting prompts
- schema_valid_rate >= 90% for core prompts
- document common repairs and include them in the model card

Open questions / experiments to add later:
- Should we include a set of deliberately maliciously formatted prompts (injection-style) and measure sanitizer effectiveness?
- Integrate a quick-fix transformer that rewrites responses into strict JSON using a small deterministic model and measure downstream improvement.

Appendix: short example run log (truncated)
- prompt: WHITESPACE_NOISE_01, temp=0.0, repeat=1
- raw: "\n {  \"id\"  :  \"txn_123\" ,\n    \"status\" : \"ok\",  \n    \"items\": [ {\"name\":\"widget\", \"qty\":3}, ] }\n"
- parse_error: trailing comma at items[0]
- repaired: stripped trailing comma -> parsed ok (mark as repaired)
- schema_valid: true (after repair)

If you use this prompt-set, please copy this doc into the model's onboarding folder and attach the harness output JSON artifact and a short triage note.

Contact: Maya Chen (applied-ml) — ping in #applied-ml when you start a run so we can coordinate triage.
